LSE 0.5.6 makes Loom the default kernel dialect on every platform, so `lse-server` starts on Linux without `--dialect`. It adds matrix-core kernels for RDNA3.5 (gfx1151, Radeon 8060S), which 0.5.5 could not start on, and decodes faster with MTP=3 (+4.5%) and DFlash2 (+1.5%). This release carries a Linux x86_64 asset again.

**Requires mac_linuxgpu v0.1.151 (build 255) or later** on macOS. Kernel arguments in VRAM need **v0.1.161 (build 265)**, as in 0.5.5. The macOS measurements below were taken on v0.1.162 (build 266), with 0.5.5 measured on the same driver.

**Load time and memory work as in 0.5.5.** The server makes every request shape's kernels resident before it reports ready. With the kernel cache on disk, the pinned DFlash2 configuration loads in 10.0 s, 0.2 s longer than 0.5.5's 9.8 s. The host memory footprint at ready is 616 MB (0.5.5: 613 MB). The first launch of a new LSE build, with none of its kernels in the cache, compiles them before it reports ready. That took 111 s with DFlash2 on the Mac and 296 s on Linux.

## Changes

1. **Loom is the default kernel dialect on every platform.** `lse`, `lse-server` and libLSE generate Loom kernels unless `--dialect hip` is named. In libLSE, a NULL `lse_config.dialect` means Loom. In 0.5.5, Linux builds defaulted to HIP, and `lse-server` without `--dialect` failed at startup on Linux while preparing kernels. The legacy HIP dialect can still be selected. `lse_estimate` with no dialect reports fragmented K/V storage. FlashPrefill V2 and BLASST no longer need `--dialect loom` named, and are refused only with `--dialect hip`. A user primitive that spells only HIP source runs on the host interpreter unless `--dialect hip` is named, as on macOS. The CI smoke script waits up to 1200 s (`LSE_SMOKE_READY_SECONDS`) for a first launch to finish compiling its kernels; on Linux that took about 400 s for the smoke model.
2. **RDNA3.5 (gfx1151) matrix cores.** Each architecture's tuning rules and matrix-instruction rows now live in their own headers: `include/lse/dispatch/arch/{gfx1201,gfx1151,generic}.hpp` and `include/lse/math/matrix_{rdna3,rdna4,cdna3}.hpp`. The Loom dialect spells the RDNA3/3.5 WMMA rows. With them, gfx1151 runs these on its own WMMA instructions:
   - the 4-bit prefill GEMM
   - the flash prefill attention
   - the 4-row and 8-row int8 decode panels

   gfx1151 also splits decode attention across the part, and runs MTP and DFlash2 verify passes on the shared int8 panel. The prefill GEMM's wide tile is chosen per part. The Q6 staged-bf16 kernels, the 64-row prefill panel tiles and FP8 WMMA are RDNA4-only; gfx1151 uses the generic contraction there. The gfx1151 work leaves gfx1201's kernel sources and greedy output unchanged.
3. **Faster verify passes.** In an 8-row verify pass, the k and v projections read the shared activation panel. In a 4-row (MTP=3) pass, the k, v and gated-delta-net a and b projections read it too. Each 4-row down-projection wave now computes two adjacent columns. A 640-token decode on the R9700 runs at 58.8 tok/s with MTP=3, up from 56.2 (+4.5%), and 58.7 tok/s with DFlash2, up from 57.8 (+1.5%).
4. **Offline gfx1151 capture.** `LSE_CAPTURE_TARGET=gfx1151-loom` loads a whole model and emits every request shape's kernels for gfx1151 with no GPU. With `LSE_TEST_REAL_COMPILE` it also compiles them.

Greedy (temperature 0) output on the pinned configuration is identical to 0.5.5 with DFlash2 and plain decoding.

## Performance on macOS (R9700)

Qwen3.8-27B Q4 with the Q8 DFlash2 draft on an R9700, mac_linuxgpu v0.1.162 (build 266), `--batch-size 1024 --ubatch-size 1024 --kv-cache-dtype bf16 --kv-len 262100`, `LSE_REQUIRE_DEVICE_KERNELS=1`. Cold is the first request of that size after the server starts, with the kernel cache on disk. Warm is the median of five requests that follow five more at the same size. Decode is the median of five 640-token runs after one more.

| Prompt tokens | Warm TTFT | Warm prefill | Cold TTFT | 0.5.5 warm TTFT | 0.5.5 cold TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 137 | 0.127 s | 1,079 tok/s | 0.188 s | 0.123 s | 0.188 s |
| 271 | 0.206 s | 1,316 tok/s | 0.210 s | 0.205 s | 0.206 s |
| 532 | 0.380 s | 1,400 tok/s | 0.386 s | 0.380 s | 0.385 s |
| 646 | 0.442 s | 1,462 tok/s | 0.445 s | 0.442 s | 0.444 s |
| 1060 | 0.674 s | 1,573 tok/s | 0.683 s | 0.675 s | 0.684 s |
| 2118 | 1.315 s | 1,611 tok/s | 1.343 s | 1.316 s | 1.345 s |
| 4230 | 2.637 s | 1,604 tok/s | 2.636 s | 2.636 s | 2.639 s |

Time to first token is within 1 ms of 0.5.5 at every size except 137 tokens. There a warm request takes 4 ms longer: 0.127 s against 0.123 s (-3.3%).

| Mode | 640-token decode | Draft acceptance | 2K prompt (2406 tokens) | 4K prompt (4787 tokens) | 0.5.5, 640-token decode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash2 | 58.7 tok/s | 65.5% | 60.2 tok/s, TTFT 1.50 s | 68.0 tok/s, TTFT 3.04 s | 57.8 tok/s |
| MTP=3 (`--mtp qwen38-27b-mtp-q8 --mtp-depth 3`) | 58.8 tok/s | 68.9% | 61.7 tok/s | — | 56.2 tok/s |
| Plain (`--dflash2=off`) | 31.9 tok/s | — | 31.5 tok/s, TTFT 1.50 s | — | 31.8 tok/s |

Model load, launch to ready with the checkpoint in the file cache and the kernel cache on disk: 10.0 s with DFlash2, 8.3 s plain, 3.9 s with MTP (0.5.5: 9.8, 8.1 and 4.0 s).

## Linux (R9700, ROCm 7.13)

The packaged `lse-v0.5.6-linux-x86_64` archive, run from a moved copy on an R9700 with ROCm 7.13 (Ubuntu, GCC 16.0.1, CMake 4.2.3), pinned Qwen3.8-27B Q4 configuration, default dialect, `LSE_REQUIRE_DEVICE_KERNELS=1`. Decode is the median of five 640-token runs after one more.

| Mode | 640-token decode | Draft acceptance | 0.5.5, same build host (`--dialect loom`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash2 | 50.1 tok/s | 65.5% | 49.7 tok/s |
| Plain (`--dflash2=off`) | 27.9 tok/s | — | 28.2 tok/s |

Plain decode is 0.3 tok/s slower than 0.5.5 (-1.1%); one of its five runs measured 23.2 tok/s. Load with the kernel cache on disk takes 21.5 s with DFlash2 (0.5.5: 21.8 s). A first launch, with no kernels in the cache, takes 296 s with DFlash2 and 302 s plain.

**Runtime requirements**, read from the binaries' symbol versions: glibc 2.43 or later (the bundled `libhrx` and `libloomc`), the GCC 16 libstdc++ (`GLIBCXX_3.4.35`, `CXXABI_1.3.15`), and ROCm 7.x `libamd_comgr.so.3` and `libhsa-runtime64.so.1`. That is an Ubuntu 26.04-class system. The archive bundles HRX and the patched Loom compiler. GPU targets built: `gfx942`, `gfx1150`, `gfx1151`, `gfx1200`, `gfx1201`; only gfx1201 was run for this release.

**Tests** (the release workflow's Test step on the R9700): 100 of 102 pass. The two that fail:
- `test_graph` fails 3 of 127 cases: `quant_linear_matches_the_weights_it_encodes`, `quant_embedding_gathers_the_rows_it_encodes` and `quant_linear_indexed_matches_the_expert_it_selects`. These are the same three cases that fail on macOS in 0.5.5 and 0.5.6. On Linux, 0.5.5 ran HIP and failed the first of them.
- `test_jit` fails 1 of 123 cases: `a_traffic_model_that_forgets_a_term_disagrees_with_the_object`, as in 0.5.5.

`test_model`, `test_memory_lifecycle` and `test_runtime` failed in 0.5.5 on Linux, with GPU page faults and three MTP cases. All three pass in 0.5.6. The Smoke-test step passes all 12 checks with the default dialect. Its server became ready 398 s after a first launch.

MS-S1 MAX with a Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), ROCm 7.13, Ubuntu 24.04, pinned Qwen3.8-27B Q4 configuration. 0.5.5 failed at startup on this part.

| Mode | Decode | Draft acceptance |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Plain | 13.3 tok/s (640 tokens) | — |
| MTP=3 | 15.1 tok/s | 65% |
| DFlash2 | 18.4 tok/s | 67% |

Prefill runs at 250 to 320 tok/s.
